problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩\times ⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0 \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =⟨0-0,-(-{cos}^{2}⁡3t-{sin}^{2}⁡3t),0-0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
